newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Seagate, Intel drive disk makers down.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Seagate, Intel drive disk makers down.

text.p: Shares of computer disk drive makers fell Tuesday on concerns that demand for personal computers may be slowing.

A warning on Monday from Seagate after the market close that its fourth quarter earnings could be weaker than expected sent Seagate shares lower but it was comments from Intel Corp. at their annual analyst meeting on Tuesday that kept the disk drive sector lower.

Shares of Seagate Technology Inc. fell 3-1/4 to 39-1/8 in afternoon trading while rival Western Digital Corp. shed 2-1/2 to 55-3/4, both on the New York Stock Exchange. Another disk drive maker Quantum Corp. lost 1-1/4 to 38-5/8 on Nasdaq. Intel shares dropped 4-3/4 to 145.
Intel's comments concerning poor European demand supported the downtrend for the high techs, analysts said.

"My concern is with people like Intel saying that demand is weak in Europe and potentially spreading and other signs of weakness from a host of other companies," David Takata, analyst at Gruntal & Co. said.
At its annual meeting with analysts in New York, Intel said it was too soon to say whether the decline in Intel's European chip sales will translate into an entire PC sector decline.
"There is some concern in general about the health of the PC industry and it's just started to show up ... and more and more people are getting concerned," Takata said.

"People have mistaken Compaq Computer Corp. and Dell Computer Corp.'s strength as indicators of the overall health of the PC industry when these two companies are probably just gaining (market) share," Takata said.
Compaq, the world's largest personal computer maker, said last week that it had a strong April and May and demand in Europe was robust adding it was bullish for the rest of the year.

Western Digital also issued an upbeat outlook for the quarter, telling investors it is comfortable with Wall Street analyst's earnings forecasts for its fourth quarter, ending in June, of $1.85 a share to $1.95 a share.
The consensus among analysts is for Western Digital to report fourth quarter earnings of $1.92 a share, according to a First Call survey.
However, the market seemed to focus instead on the more negative news from Seagate and Intel.

Seagate, one of the nation's largest makers of disk drives, on Monday said fourth quarter revenues are expected to be between 6 percent and 10 percent below the $2.5 billion reported for the third quarter ended in March. The company also said earnings before one-time charges could fall short of the third quarter's profit of $1.01 a share.
Wall Street analysts had expected Seagate to earn $1.06 a share in its fourth quarter, according to First Call.
Seagate attributed the shortfall to new competition from companies like Western Digital and Quantum which was eroding its market share at the high-end of the disk drive market

Seagate's warning fueled fears that the PC market may be slowing, particularly overseas. But Seagate's Chairman, President and Chief Executive Al Shugard said Monday he saw no weakness in the PC sector and demand still far outstrips supply of disk drives.
Andrew Neff, analyst at Bear Stearns & Co. said much of the problem is just jitters in the high technology stocks.
"It's a broaad technology weakness," he said.

Todd Bakar, an analyst at Hambrecht & Quist said that the comments from Seagate, Intel and Cabletron Systems Inc., which said on Monday it would not meet earnings estimates, were affecting the broader technology sector.
"The overall tone in the disk drive industry is tougher today was it was a month or two ago," Bakar said.

"With companies like Intel, Seagate and Cabletron on the communications side, you have three big companies early in the quarter announcing disappointments that is clearly creating a sell-off of all technology stocks," he said.
Cabletron said Monday it expects to report first-quarter earnings per share of about $0.37, equaling or slightly exceeding its year-ago results but falling below analysts' expectations.

The First Call consensus estimate for Cabletron's first quarter of fiscal 1998 was $0.50 a share. Shares of Cabletron lost about a third of its value falling 15-1/8 to 30-3/8 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
